security_spec.violation_condition: The mseccfg.MML WARL field in the CSR module is implemented as a standard writable register without sticky-bit semantics. When software writes 1 then 0 to MML, the hardware allows the clear operation without requiring a PMP reset. This violates the normative rule that MML is a sticky bit that 'once set it cannot be unset until a PMP reset.' In Chisel, this means the MML bit is driven by a simple Reg(Wire) that accepts any CSR write value rather than a RegInit(0.B) with write-side conditioning that blocks 1→0 transitions unless a reset signal is asserted. The PMP checker logic then incorrectly transitions from Smepmp enforcement mode back to legacy PMP mode, re-enabling M-mode's unrestricted access to all physical memory that was previously locked down.
security_spec.summary: Non-sticky mseccfg.MML implementation allows M-mode to clear MML by CSR write, escaping Smepmp lockdown and regaining unrestricted physical memory access without a PMP reset
